note: WHAT A RENDER MANIFEST MAY CONTAIN, DECLARED ONCE. The preparer (test/corpus/prep/manifest.py) and the runner (test/render/Parity.cpp) both read this file and neither restates it: a key that exists here exists for both, and a key that does not exists for neither. Two closed sets over one declaration is what this file replaces -- they disagreed on eight of twenty-six manifests and nothing failed. Cross-field POLICY is not here: which Cycles settings are refused belongs to the preparer, which thresholds may be overridden and which lights the studio can build belong to the runner. This file declares only what a key IS.

types.index: a whole number, zero or above
types.opaque: a non-empty object whose interior this schema does not declare, because its reader gives it meaning -- the fixture recipes and the Blender export settings
types.{object: name}: the object declared under that name
types.{array: type}: a non-empty list of that type
types.{map: type}: a non-empty object whose keys are arbitrary and whose values are that type
types.{quantity: type}: value of that type, with unit, origin and -- where derived -- derivation
types.filename: a plain file name in the case directory: no slash and no leading dot

manifest.note: THE ONLY TRACKED FILE IN A CASE DIRECTORY (board:0083): the scene, the recipe and the acceptance in one declaration.

threshold-override.note: A manifest's `acceptance` block carries only what it OVERRIDES over the suite's declared defaults, so every entry owes a reason. WHICH keys may be overridden is the runner's, because the defaults are the runner's.

self-describing.note: `oracleRole` AND ITS TWO COMPANIONS SAY WHAT CYCLES CANNOT EXPRESS ABOUT THIS CRITERION AND WHAT THAT COSTS. A role of cannot-express-the-criterion without a limitation, or a limitation with no measurement beside it, is the runner's refusal.

criterion.note: THREE KINDS OF CRITERION AND THE KIND DECIDES THE INSTRUMENT (board:0085). `numeric` -- the asset states a value or a relation and the acceptance is that number on the linear tap. `self-describing` -- the asset renders checkmarks, arrows or markers whose correctness is readable FROM THE PICTURE. `stated-invariant` -- the asset states a relation between two parts of its own render. `limits-probe` -- the asset states it is not expected to render correctly everywhere and has no pass at all.

depth-probe.note: WHICH SURFACE THE PICTURE IS OF, in metres along the view ray at one named pixel. Silhouette, coverage and hue are all invariant under swapping the near shell of a closed body for its far one with the normals reversed -- three criteria simultaneously blind, each individually correct (board:0073). Depth is not invariant under it, it costs one assertion, and `Renderer::ReadDepth` already provides it. `atPx` is column then row from the TOP-left, the raster's own origin.

subject-patch.note: A CORRECTION APPLIED BETWEEN THE FETCH AND THE ORACLE, so the upstream pin stays exact and both sides render the same corrected bytes (board:0095). It is a DELTA and never a replacement: the fetch still verifies upstream's sha256, so a change upstream is still a refusal, and the patched product is what the oracle key covers. `stillTests` is the boundary that stops patching becoming an escape hatch -- the asset's own criterion must be the same sentence after the patch, and a correction that changes what the asset TESTS is a re-authoring. `retirementCondition` is a predicate the suite already evaluates rather than a wish.

reverse-winding.note: Swaps the second and third corner of every triangle of a primitive whose faces point inward, and moves no vertex. `observedBefore` is the state it expects to find and the preparer RECOMPUTES it: `triangles`, `trianglesCounterClockwiseFromOutside` and `trianglesOfZeroArea`. That is what makes the measurement load-bearing rather than decorative, and it is also the RETIREMENT PREDICATE: when upstream corrects the asset the declared count no longer matches what is on disk and the run goes red, so a fork cannot be carried for ever by nobody's decision. Applying the patch twice refuses for the same reason.

flip-normals.note: Negates every vertex normal of a primitive whose normals point inward, and touches no position and no index. `observedBefore` carries `vertexNormals` and `vertexNormalsOutward`, recomputed the same way and refused on mismatch.

subject-transform.note: ONE NAMED CORRECTION WITH ITS PARAMETERS, never a free-form edit: an arbitrary transform is a re-authoring and cannot be reviewed, a named one can. Winding and normals are TWO corrections and not one, because they are two independent defects that happened to occur together -- an asset with one of them is a case this list still describes. A patch expressible as a text diff of the JSON is the natural third kind; these two are not, because the defect they answer lives in the binary buffer.

generated-file.note: No url, no pin and no licence: there is no upstream to pin against and no third party to credit. What stands in the pin's place is that the recipe is the whole of the input, so the preparer digests what it produced.

licence.note: Per file and never per repository: a repository-level claim covers nothing in particular.

gltf.note: THE INDEX INTO THE FILE'S OWN `cameras`, AND IT HAS NO DEFAULT. `Cameras` puts a perspective and an orthographic camera on two nodes at one point, so "the camera the file carries" names nothing there; a case that adopted the first would render one of them and report the other's criterion.

manifest.note: A PARALLEL PROJECTION IS A DIFFERENT MATRIX AND NOT A LONG LENS, so it is declared and never inferred from which field happens to be present. The orthographic arm carries the vertical extent it covers and no field of view at all.

gltf.note: `lightingMode` IS HOW THE IMPORTER TURNS glTF'S PHOTOMETRIC UNITS INTO BLENDER'S RADIOMETRIC ONES. RAW takes `intensity` across unchanged, correct for a directional light where glTF's lux IS Blender's Sun Strength one to one; for a point light RAW makes candela into WATTS OF TOTAL POWER and Cycles radiates energy/4pi per steradian, a factor of 4pi below the extension's definition, so COMPAT is the arm that makes candela mean candela. `estimator` says whether the oracle still has one: `delta` is a scene whose only source has no area, so two seeds must agree bit for bit; `selected` is a scene with more than one such light, where Cycles picks ONE per shading event and which one is the seed's business.

sun.note: `estimator` ON THIS ARM CANNOT SAY `selected` AND THAT IS THE POINT: this arm declares ONE source, the preparer refuses an `angleRad` above zero, and `no_surface_of_the_subject_is_a_light` takes the subject's own emission out of the light tree and out of every gathering ray -- so a sun-lit case has no estimator left and no way to say it has one. Three cases said `selected` here and none of them may any more. MEASURED at Blender 5.2.0, 1280x720, 1 spp, box filter 0.01, black world, zero bounces, angular diameter zero, seed 0 against seed 1: BINARY colour samples BEFORE the reduction -- WaterBottle 67 578, BoomBox 55 496, Lantern 22 120, Corset 0 -- and AFTER it, 0 on all four, alpha identical throughout. NEITHER HALF ALONE REACHES ZERO: `emission_sampling = NONE` alone leaves 222 samples over 74 pixels on Lantern and 42 over 15 on BoomBox, every one where a BSDF-sampled direction finds the lit glass; ray visibility alone leaves 67 575 on WaterBottle, which refutes the guess that an object invisible to diffuse and glossy rays leaves Cycles' light tree. `not-bit-reproducible` IS NOT A SECOND ESTIMATOR AND NOT A TOLERANCE -- it is the case saying the HOST does not reproduce this subject's own render, so the two-seed check has nothing to speak through; it owes its measurement the same way and it refuses the second recipe rather than tolerating a difference in it. `hostResidueRelative` IS WHAT `not-bit-reproducible` OWES AND THE RUNNER REFUSES THE WORD WITHOUT IT: the worst relative disagreement between two renders of this scene on this host, measured, because the picture bound (board:0089) derives a term in display codes from it and a case that claimed the word without the number would be claiming room nobody measured.

light.note: WHY TWO SEEDS MIGHT NOT AGREE, AND `delta` IS THE CLAIM THAT THEY MUST: one source with no area, nothing else in Cycles' light tree, and the two dumps identical bit for bit. THE OTHER TWO NAME WHAT STANDS IN THE WAY, each with its measurement beside it in the case's own note. `selected` -- more than one sampled source, where Cycles picks ONE per shading event and which one is the seed's business -- is spellable ONLY on the `gltf` arm, where the number of lights is the FILE's and no setting of ours changes it. AN EMISSIVE SURFACE USED TO BE COUNTED AMONG THOSE SOURCES AND IS NOT ONE ANY MORE: the preparer takes the subject out of the light tree and out of every gathering ray, so a declared sun is a delta scene by construction. `not-bit-reproducible` -- the HOST does not reproduce this subject's render at a FIXED seed, so bit-identity is not a question about the estimator here at all. It replaced `filter-sample`, which named the single sample's position inside the pixel as what moved Corset between two seeds; the measurement that retired that word is that Corset's pixels move between two runs at the SAME seed and not between two seeds.

world.note: `factory` is Blender's own environment and its number is not a manifest's to restate; `uniform` is the arm a case takes to REMOVE the environment, because an environment is an area source and a delta light is not.

emission.note: ONE COLOUR PER NODE, AND NO SHORTER SPELLING. Flat emission over touching bodies fuses them into one silhouette, so a misplaced node hides inside the union. A map keyed by the file's own name is what makes "the third cube" a fact about the file instead of a position in a list.

emission-per-material.note: THE MATERIAL IS THE KEY A MULTI-MATERIAL ASSET HAS: a mesh whose primitives name different materials is one Blender object with several slots, so a per-object colour could reach only one of them.

material.note: WHICH SURFACE THE COMPARISON IS OVER, and the (source, kind) pairs below are the whole set. "gltf" hands the format its own metal-rough row entire; a `diffuse` arm over it would silently discard two of the three inputs. "gltf-base-colour" LOWERS THE ORACLE RATHER THAN THE TOLERANCE (board:0087): the imported Principled BSDF carries a specular lobe at IOR 1.5 whatever the metallic factor, so a textured asset rendered with it has an integral left and no closed form to be judged against -- this arm keeps the file's own image, uv set and sampler and replaces the closure. "gltf-emissive" is the same arm over the other socket, and it has ONE closure: glTF's emission is a radiance the surface leaves, not a reflectance an environment multiplies into.

stated-invariant.note: THE RELATION THE ASSET STATES ABOUT A RENDER OF ITSELF, evaluated on the scene-referred linear tap and on nothing else. `hue-of-brightest` -- over the brightest declared fraction of the covered pixels, each channel's share of the pixel's own sum equals a declared hue. `region-compare` -- two rectangles of the frame, congruent by construction, agree per channel after a declared scale. A region-compare carries EXACTLY ONE currency and the runner refuses both or neither: `maxUlps` is a maximum and is right where both sides come out of one shader over one surface, `maxP95Relative` is a quantile and is the only honest currency where the two regions are the same surface stated two ways -- a tessellation against a bake of it disagrees by O(1) on the silhouette rim for a correct renderer.
